i) mixed infection of PPRV and foot and mouth disease virus (FDMV) is possible; ii) viral interference between PPEV and FMD is possible; iii) persistence of PPRV is more than that of FMDV; iv) viral persistence may modify viral persistence; and v) mixed infection of FDMV and PPR virus is possible in goats.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, purification and molecular characterization of two important viral pathogens of livestock, namely PPRV and foot and mouth disease virus (FDMV) in mixed infections in goats.
a novel strategy to eliminate a negative-stranded RNA (NS RNA) virus from a virus mixture and the study of viral interference and persistence in mixed infections.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the virus mixtures could be purified and characterized by plaque assay, transfection and long-term co-infection in cell culture systems.
mixed viral infections are complex, but not impossible to handle.
mixed infections of PPRV and other acute pathogenic viruses may be a potential source of viral interference, persistence and exclusion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mixed infections are not always a bad thing.
the virus isolation from mixed infection is a complex process and requires a careful consideration of the nature and characteristics of the viruses in the mixture.
the virus isolation, purification and persistence are highly influenced by the cell type, virus strain, and the nature of mixed infection.
